commonPrompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production 2D combat VFX overlay sprite sheet for AlarmQuest. Create exactly 16 chronological animation frames in a strict 4-column by 4-row, row-major sprite sheet. Every cell is an independent wide 361:160 combat viewport; final sheet 1444:640; Detailed hand-painted high-resolution 2D rendering; transparent RGBA; fixed camera, fixed scale, clean antialiased alpha, image-rendering auto, no pixel art. This is the warrior's first and weakest skill, but it must feel authored rather than empty: use three restrained, clearly separated layers—one razor core, one translucent steel-pressure ribbon, and one broken parallel wake—plus a compact contact structure. Motion grammar: LOCKED_SPLINE_TOP_DOWN_CUT. Define one immutable descending cubic Bézier centerline for the entire sheet: P0=(37%,8%), P1=(39%,31%), P2=(51%,59%), P3=(61%,80%). The cutting direction is unmistakably top to bottom with a modest left-to-right diagonal. Never redraw, rotate, bend, scale, or horizontally shift this centerline between frames. If all frames were overlaid, every razor-core pixel must lie on the same single spline. Animate only a short reveal mask traveling monotonically downward along that fixed spline. The visible main segment has a constant arc length of 20-24% of the full spline after F04; its leading tip moves downward every frame and its trailing end disappears on the same path. Keep core thickness constant at 2-3 px and the steel-pressure ribbon at 8-12 px. A broken parallel wake may sit 3-5% left of the core, always tangent and parallel to the same spline; it must not wander independently. Frame choreography: F01 almost clear. F02-F04 reveal a short upper entry notch at curve parameters t=0.06, 0.12, 0.19. F05-F08 move the leading tip through t=0.27, 0.35, 0.43, 0.51 while preserving identical curvature and thickness. F09-F12 continue through t=0.59, 0.67, 0.75, 0.83; add two short tapered pressure facets behind the ribbon so the cut is richer but not magical. F13-F15 continue through t=0.89, 0.94, 0.98 and compress visibly toward P3 without contact. F16 at 937.5-1000ms is the only impact at the immutable point P3=(61%,80%): the descending razor core terminates against one short diagonal resistance plate, folds into a compact hooked steel wedge two to three times the core thickness, and ejects four to six tiny triangular steel chips with two muted amber sparks. Keep the core, ribbon, wake, and impact wedge visually connected as one physical cut. Stop on F16; there are no frames after contact and no finisher. The full moving effect may occupy x=29-69% and y=4-88%, but overall alpha occupancy must stay low with broad transparent space. Palette: cold gunmetal, desaturated blue-gray pressure, ivory razor edge, and tiny muted amber contact accents. Treat each cell as a separately clipped final viewport with no neighboring-frame residue. Render only VFX; no character, enemy, weapon body, scenery, ground, UI, text, labels, grid, borders, gutters, padding, or opaque background.

skills.name: 칼날 베기
skills.generationPrompt: Regenerate ‘칼날 베기’ from scratch as a stable descending physical cut. Do not use either rejected sheet as an image reference. The dominant reading must be a blade-pressure edge entering from the upper part of the viewport and slicing downward into a lower-right contact. Temporal stability is the primary quality target: reuse the exact same immutable Bézier path, tangent, curvature, core thickness, and final contact point in all 16 cells; animate only the reveal window along that path. Each successive active frame must move the leading tip farther downward without any left-right correction or angle change. Make the effect less simplistic using three coordinated layers: a thin ivory razor core, a broader translucent gunmetal pressure ribbon with two deliberate triangular gaps, and a shorter desaturated-blue parallel wake offset to the left. These layers must share the same tangent and read as one sword swing, not three attacks. On F16 alone, turn the lower tip into a compact hooked contact wedge against a short opposing steel plate, with four to six tiny chips and only two amber sparks. The contact must feel firm at native 361x160 size but remain clearly weaker than later warrior skills. Stop exactly at impact with no explosion, ring, recovery, residue, second hit, or finishing phase. VFX only; no body, sword object, enemy, ground, scenery, UI, or lettering.
